messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@atlashealth.com>, Lina Gomez <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: staged capacity ramp & billing schedule (AWS + GCP)

Hi Samir / Lina,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get Atlas over the line. Per our conversation, attached is a recommended activation plan that will let you start with a conservative commit and ramp as usage normalizes (this helps keep unit costs predictable while giving your engineering teams room to scale).

High-level proposal:
- Term: 12 months, effective on first acceptance date (target acceptance window: 2027-11-01 to 2027-11-07).
- Capacity staging (monthly uptime targets / committed units):
  - Month 1-2: 50k seq-token equivalents / day (baseline)
  - Month 3-4: 100k seq-token equivalents / day
  - Month 5+: 150k seq-token equivalents / day (final committed level)
- Marketplace split: AWS Private Offer (primary) + GCP Private Offer (secondary) for regional failover. Billing will be presented as two vendor invoices but we can coordinate consolidated invoicing in tranches.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly with option for 3-tranche pre-pay invoice (if you prefer). Proration applies only to the month of activation.
- Acceptance: functional acceptance checklist + 7-day usage validation window (we will publish acceptance events to the private-offer record).

Attachments sent with this message: 1) Atlas_Demand_Projection_2027Q4Q1.xlsx (demand profile we discussed) 2) Draft_PO_AWS_Atlas_0412.pdf (template PO for AWS private offer).

Action items for Atlas: please confirm whether you can: 1) sign the PO as-is or provide legal redlines, 2) confirm the acceptance window above, and 3) indicate preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. 3-tranche).

If that looks good I'll loop in Finance & Legal here at Redwood to prepare final private-offer artifacts for AWS and GCP and will coordinate DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Marketplace & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Tessa,

Thanks — we reviewed the plan internally. A few clarifying questions before procurement executes: 

1) Can Redwood provide a single PO that covers both AWS and GCP private offers, or do we need separate POs per marketplace? We prefer a single PO but understand marketplace constraints.

2) Tax handling — will Redwood apply tax on each marketplace invoice or do you have a consolidated tax treatment? We need tax line-item language for our AP team.

3) Acceptance — the checklist looks fine. For our legal/audit records we need an acceptance artefact (signed checklist or confirmation email) that we can tie to the private-offer acceptance event. Can Redwood generate that automatically once acceptance criteria are met?

4) Billing tranches — we like the 3-tranche invoice option for budgeting. Please confirm whether invoices will be dated at acceptance or issued at start of each tranche period.

I'm attaching our signed PO template (for your countersign). We redlined a single point of clarification on proration; otherwise it is ready.

Lina
Lina Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager, Atlas Health

Subject: Re: Private offer: staged capacity ramp & billing schedule (AWS + GCP)

Lina — really appreciate the quick turnaround and the signed PO. Answers inline below (and attaching an updated PO + acceptance checklist with the proration language tightened per your note):

On Wed, Sep 29, 2027 at 11:10 AM Lina Gomez <procurement@atlashealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Single PO or separate?
We can accept a single master PO that references both marketplace private offers. Operationally we will still publish two private-offer artifacts (one in AWS, one in GCP), but the PO can be the single contract reference for your AP team.

> 2) Tax handling
Redwood will apply tax based on the marketplace jurisdiction of each invoice (AWS invoice taxed per AWS rules; GCP invoice taxed per GCP rules). We will add an explicit tax line and provide tax jurisdiction meta on each invoice. If you require consolidated tax reporting, Finance can provide a monthly consolidated statement for your records.

> 3) Acceptance artefact generation
Yes — Redwood will auto-generate an acceptance confirmation email and PDF (signed by our program manager) once the checklist finishes and the 7-day validation window closes. That document will be attached to the private-offer record and we will push the acceptance event to the DocuSign summary and HubSpot deal.

> 4) Billing tranches timing
Invoices will be issued at tranche start dates. For example, if tranche 1 begins on 2027-11-01, invoice 1 will be dated 2027-11-01. Proration language is included for partial months in the updated PO.

Next steps (what we'll do on our side):
- Ben will prepare the invoice templates and tax breakdown for both marketplaces.
- Marcus will coordinate with Cloud Partnerships to schedule creation of both private offers and set the acceptance metadata.
- I'll circulate the updated PO (attached) and the acceptance checklist for your countersign.

Attached: Redwood_Acceptance_Checklist.pdf, Updated_PO_Atlas_Redwood_0930.pdf

If everything looks good please countersign the updated PO and we'll start the private-offer creation flow.

Cheers,
Tessa
